description: An introduction to matter, its three states and their properties, the particle (kinetic) theory, changes of state, physical versus chemical changes, and the difference between elements, compounds and mixtures.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is the best definition of matter?

options.text: Anything that can be seen by the eyes
Anything that has mass and occupies space
Anything that can be touched by the hands
Anything that produces heat and light

mcq.explanation: Matter is defined as anything that has mass and occupies space (has volume), whether or not it can be seen or touched.

mcq.questionText: Which one of the following is NOT a state of matter?
mcq.explanation: The three common states of matter are solid, liquid and gas. Energy is not a form of matter because it has no mass.

mcq.questionText: In which state of matter are the particles packed very closely together in a fixed, regular arrangement?
mcq.explanation: In a solid the particles are very close and held in a fixed regular pattern, which gives solids a definite shape and volume.

mcq.questionText: Why can gases be compressed much more easily than solids and liquids?

options.text: Gas particles are lighter than solid particles
Gas particles are smaller than solid particles
Gas particles have large spaces between them
Gas particles do not move at all

mcq.explanation: Gas particles are far apart with large empty spaces between them, so they can be pushed closer together (compressed) easily.

mcq.questionText: The change of state directly from a solid to a gas without passing through the liquid state is called:
mcq.explanation: Sublimation is the direct change of a solid into a gas (for example, dry ice or iodine) without first becoming a liquid.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a physical change?
mcq.explanation: Melting of ice is a physical change because no new substance is formed and it can be reversed by freezing the water again.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a chemical change?
mcq.explanation: Burning of wood is a chemical change because new substances such as ash, smoke and gases are formed and it cannot be easily reversed.

mcq.questionText: The process by which a liquid changes into a gas is called:
mcq.explanation: Evaporation (or boiling) is the change of a liquid into a gas as the particles gain energy and escape from the liquid surface.

mcq.questionText: A substance that is made of only one kind of atom and cannot be broken down into simpler substances is called:
mcq.explanation: An element is a pure substance made of only one type of atom and cannot be broken down into simpler substances by chemical means.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a compound?
mcq.explanation: Water is a compound because it is made of two different elements (hydrogen and oxygen) chemically combined in a fixed ratio.

mcq.questionText: Which statement correctly describes the particles in a liquid according to the kinetic theory?

options.text: They are far apart and move very fast in all directions
They are close together but can slide past one another
They are fixed in position and only vibrate
They do not move at all

mcq.explanation: In a liquid the particles are close together but are free to move and slide over one another, so a liquid flows and takes the shape of its container.

mcq.questionText: Air, soil and sea water are all examples of:
mcq.explanation: Air, soil and sea water are mixtures because they contain two or more substances that are not chemically combined and can be separated physically.

mcq.questionText: When water vapour in the air cools and turns into liquid water droplets, the process is called:
mcq.explanation: Condensation is the change of a gas (water vapour) into a liquid when it loses heat and the particles move closer together.

mcq.questionText: Which property is shared by ALL three states of matter?

options.text: They have mass and occupy space
Their particles are fixed in position

mcq.explanation: Although shape and compressibility differ, all matter in any state has mass and occupies space, which is the defining property of matter.

mcq.questionText: A liquid has a definite volume but no definite shape because its particles:

options.text: Are very far apart and move freely
Are held tightly in fixed positions
Are close together but free to move around

mcq.explanation: The particles of a liquid are close enough to keep a fixed volume but are free to move, so the liquid takes the shape of its container.

fib.questionText: Anything that has mass and occupies space is called _____.
fib.explanation: Matter is the general term for anything that has mass and takes up space.

fib.questionText: The three common states of matter are solid, liquid and _____.
fib.explanation: Matter usually exists in three states: solid, liquid and gas.

fib.questionText: The change of a solid into a liquid when it is heated is called _____.
fib.explanation: Melting (or fusion) is the change of state from solid to liquid as the particles gain heat energy.

fib.questionText: The change of a liquid into a solid when it is cooled is called _____.
fib.explanation: Freezing (solidification) is the change of state from liquid to solid as particles lose heat energy.

fib.questionText: The theory that explains the behaviour of matter in terms of tiny moving particles is called the _____ theory.
fib.explanation: The kinetic (particle) theory states that all matter is made of tiny particles that are constantly moving.

fib.questionText: A change in which no new substance is formed and which can usually be reversed is called a _____ change.
fib.explanation: Physical changes, such as melting or dissolving, do not form new substances and are usually reversible.

fib.questionText: A change in which one or more new substances are formed is called a _____ change.
fib.explanation: Chemical changes, such as burning or rusting, form new substances and are usually difficult to reverse.

fib.questionText: A pure substance made of two or more elements chemically joined together is called a _____.
fib.explanation: A compound is formed when different elements combine chemically in a fixed ratio, for example water and carbon dioxide.

fib.questionText: Two or more substances that are physically combined and can be separated again form a _____.
fib.explanation: A mixture contains substances that are not chemically joined, so they can be separated by physical methods.

fib.questionText: The direct change of a gas into a solid without becoming a liquid is called _____.
fib.explanation: Deposition is the reverse of sublimation, where a gas changes straight into a solid, for example frost forming from water vapour.

tf.questionText: All matter is made up of tiny particles that are in constant motion.
tf.explanation: According to the kinetic theory, matter is made of tiny particles that are always moving.

tf.questionText: Solids can be compressed easily because their particles are far apart.
tf.explanation: Solid particles are packed very closely with almost no spaces, so solids cannot be compressed easily.

tf.questionText: Melting of ice is a physical change.
tf.explanation: Melting ice only changes the state of water; no new substance is formed and it can be reversed by freezing.

tf.questionText: Burning of paper is a reversible change.
tf.explanation: Burning is a chemical change that forms new substances such as ash and gases and cannot be reversed.

tf.questionText: Gases have a definite shape and a definite volume.
tf.explanation: Gases have neither a definite shape nor a definite volume; they fill any container completely.
Water is a compound because it is made of two elements, hydrogen and oxygen, chemically combined.

tf.questionText: A mixture can be separated into its components by physical methods.
tf.explanation: Because the substances in a mixture are not chemically joined, they can be separated by physical methods such as filtering or evaporation.

tf.questionText: During condensation a gas changes into a liquid.
tf.explanation: Condensation occurs when a gas loses heat and its particles come closer together to form a liquid.

tf.questionText: In a liquid, the particles are completely fixed in position and cannot move.
tf.explanation: Liquid particles are close together but free to move and slide past one another, which is why liquids flow.

tf.questionText: Heating generally makes the particles of a substance move faster and move further apart.
tf.explanation: Heating gives particles more energy, making them move faster and increasing the spaces between them.

summary.correctAnswer: Matter is anything that has mass and occupies space.
summary.explanation: This is the core idea of the whole topic and applies to every substance around us.

summary.correctAnswer: Matter exists as solid, liquid and gas.
summary.explanation: Each state differs in the arrangement and movement of its particles.

summary.correctAnswer: A solid has a definite shape and a definite volume and cannot be compressed.
summary.explanation: Its particles are closely packed in fixed positions and only vibrate.

summary.correctAnswer: A liquid has a definite volume but takes the shape of its container.
summary.explanation: Its particles are close together but free to move and slide over each other.

summary.correctAnswer: A gas has no definite shape or volume and can be compressed easily.
summary.explanation: Its particles are far apart and move quickly in all directions.

summary.correctAnswer: All matter is made of tiny particles that are always moving.
summary.explanation: The arrangement, spacing and speed of the particles explain the properties of each state.

summary.correctAnswer: A physical change forms no new substance and is usually reversible.
summary.explanation: Examples include melting, freezing, boiling and dissolving.

summary.correctAnswer: A chemical change forms new substances and is usually not easily reversed.
summary.explanation: Examples include burning, rusting and the souring of milk.

summary.correctAnswer: Melting, freezing, evaporation, condensation, sublimation and deposition are changes of state.
summary.explanation: They happen when matter gains or loses heat energy, changing how the particles are arranged.

summary.correctAnswer: An element has one kind of atom, a compound has elements chemically joined, and a mixture has substances physically combined.
summary.explanation: Compounds have fixed compositions, while mixtures can be separated by physical methods.

hoq.questionText: A student leaves a small bowl of water and a similar bowl of cooking oil outside on a hot, sunny day. After several hours the water level has dropped much more than the oil level. Which conclusion best explains this observation?

options.text: Oil is not made of particles, so it cannot evaporate
Water particles escape into the air more easily than oil particles at the same temperature
The sun only heats water and never heats oil
Water gained mass while oil lost mass

hoq.explanation: Both liquids evaporate, but water evaporates faster because its particles escape into the air more easily, so its level drops more.

hoq.questionText: A sealed syringe contains some air. When the plunger is pushed in, the air inside takes up a smaller space, but when the same is tried with a syringe full of water, the plunger hardly moves. What does this best demonstrate?

options.text: Air has no mass while water has mass
Gas particles have large spaces between them while liquid particles are close together
Water particles are larger than air particles
Air is a compound and water is an element

hoq.explanation: Gases compress because their particles have large gaps, while liquid particles are already close together and have very little space to be squeezed into.

hoq.questionText: A student heats a blue solid in a test tube. A gas is given off, the solid turns white, and water droplets collect at the cooler top of the tube. The student cannot easily get the original blue solid back. Which statement is the most correct interpretation?

options.text: Only a physical change happened because water appeared
A chemical change happened because a new substance was formed and it is hard to reverse
No change happened because the mass stayed the same
The blue solid melted and then froze again

hoq.explanation: The colour change, gas given off and difficulty in reversing the process all show that a new substance formed, which indicates a chemical change.
